cases.tierRationale: The observable is a rule's justification, not a run's output. The step cites no decision record, so no citation check reaches it: catching it requires reading the step's rule against the decision register and recognising that its authority was superseded. There is no exit status, artifact or output string that separates a live rule from a retired one, so pushing this case to the deterministic tier would mean asserting a cue that does not exist.
cases.title: A step keeps applying a rule whose governing decision was retired
verification: #4664 observed while staging the fabrika campaign: ten of the eleven wave issues were p0 and would have been demoted by the ritual as written.
ADR 0214 carries status: superseded by 0219, and ADR 0219's non-goals exclude capping campaign-homed work at p1.

cases.title: A 200 response publishes the literal path instead of the file's text
verification: #4683 was filed from two live occurrences in one session: one leaked a local path, one posted an empty finding.
#3945 carries a KEEP-AS-EVAL row on the #4634 verdict table and is absent from the 153-issue kill list on #4642.

cases.title: A fail-closed guard returns success under a non-default IFS
verification: Recorded as an eval case on #4675 (comment 5153256843) from the two-lane verification of the #4500 lane-stamp fix.
Reproduced in both directions against common.sh at d80233b0 under env -i, varying only IFS: rc 3 under the default, rc 0 under newline-only.

corrections.summary: First recorded as one of two instrumentation traps and explicitly claimed not to be a code defect. Retracted: the guard's dependence on the default IFS is a live defect in the merged lane_worktree, and the clean-shell re-run only hid it. A symptom that disappears when you clean your environment has not thereby been shown to be your environment's fault.

cases.title: A raw file write bypasses a guard that gates git mutations
verification: #3594 records two of two coder lanes writing their first edit to primary-checkout paths.
A third occurrence is disclosed in PR #4689's deviations, caught only because the commit reported two files instead of three.

cases.title: An unkeyed scratchpad leaf lets one lane commit another lane's message
verification: #4692 records the commit that landed: the file existed, was non-empty, and was a perfectly valid commit message — for the other lane.

declined.incident: a guard job reporting SUCCESS while exiting 1
declined.reason: Named as live and verified in this child's dispatch, but no citable artifact — issue, PR, commit or posted verdict — could be found for it. Admitting it would rest the corpus on recollection, which is the one thing a regression floor cannot afford. Recorded here so the omission is visible rather than silent; it enters as a case the moment an artifact is cited.
